question: The standard triple therapy regimen for H. pylori eradication (proton pump inhibitor + amoxicillin + clarithromycin for 14 days) achieves eradication rates exceeding 90% in most Indian populations.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. Clarithromycin resistance in India has risen above 15%, reducing standard triple therapy eradication rates to ~70–80%. Current guidelines recommend bismuth quadruple therapy (PPI + bismuth + tetracycline + metronidazole) or susceptibility-guided therapy in areas of high clarithromycin resistance.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct that this is false. Due to rising clarithromycin resistance in India (>15%), standard triple therapy now achieves only ~70–80% eradication rates. Bismuth-based quadruple therapy or concomitant therapy is increasingly recommended when clarithromycin resistance is prevalent.
